title: The Hidden Subgroup Problem in Semidirect Products and Quasi-Hamiltonian Groups
abstract: Several early quantum algorithms, including Simon's algorithm and Shor's period-finding are instances of the hidden subgroup problem (HSP) over finite abelian groups. No polynomial-time quantum algorithm is known for the HSP over arbitrary non-abelian finite groups. The non-Abelian case is of particular interest because some instances, such as the dihedral and symmetric group HSPs, are connected to lattice problems and graph isomorphism, respectively.   In this work, we give polynomial-time quantum algorithms for two further families containing non-Abelian groups. First, we consider groups of the form $G=A\rtimes_{\varphi} \mathbb{Z}_{p^k}$, with $A$ finite Abelian, $p$ prime, $k\in \mathbb{N}$ and the action of $\mathbb Z_{p^k}$ is generated by the scalar automorphism $a\mapstoμa$, for some $μ\in\mathbb Z_{\operatorname{Exp}(A)}^\times$, where $\mathrm{Exp}(A)$ is the exponent of $A$. Our algorithm is efficient when $A$ has bounded generator rank and $\mathrm{Exp}(A)/p=\mathrm{polylog}(|G|)$. This includes the case $A=\mathbb{Z}_N$ for $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and $k=1$, studied by Bacon, Childs and van Dam (FOCS 2005), and $A=\mathbb{Z}_{q^r}$ with $q$ prime and $r\in \mathbb{N}$ studied by van Dam and Dey (TQC 2014). Second, we give a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for finite quasi-Hamiltonian groups under a mild assumption on the input structure. Quasi-Hamiltonian groups are finite nilpotent groups with modular subgroup lattice, or equivalently the finite groups in which every subgroup is permutable. As far as we know, this is the first quantum algorithm to exploit the modularity of the subgroup lattice for solving the HSP. This extends, under the aforementioned structured input assumption, the quantum algorithm for Dedekind groups given by Hallgren, Russell, and Ta-Shma (SIAM J. Comput. 32, 2003).
summary: This paper develops polynomial-time quantum algorithms for solving the Hidden Subgroup Problem (HSP) in specific classes of non-Abelian finite groups, including semidirect products and quasi-Hamiltonian groups. It achieves this by exploiting deep structural properties of these groups and refining quantum measurement techniques like the block measurement protocol. The research advances the theoretical understanding of what computational problems can be efficiently solved on a quantum computer using group structure knowledge.
main_problem: The paper addresses the Hidden Subgroup Problem (HSP) for non-Abelian finite groups, which is significantly harder than the Abelian case.
main_result: Polynomial-time quantum algorithms are provided for two structured families of non-Abelian groups: semidirect products $A times_{\varphi} \mathbb{Z}_{p^k}$ and quasi-Hamiltonian groups.
method: The methods involve adapting techniques from Abelian HSP solvers, utilizing structural properties like modular subgroup lattices (for quasi-Hamiltonian groups), and employing advanced quantum measurement protocols like the block measurement technique.
model_or_system: The theoretical model is abstract group theory applied to quantum computation; no specific physical Hamiltonian or lattice system is described. The focus is on solving a computational problem defined over finite groups $G$.
key_observables: Success probability of the quantum algorithm, which must be shown to be high enough (e.g., $\geq  rac{\phi(N)}{N} 2^{mt} p$) for polynomial time complexity.
important_parameters: Group structure parameters such as $p$ (prime), $k$, and the exponent of the Abelian factor, $	ext{Exp}(A)$. Efficiency depends on conditions like $	ext{Exp}(A)/p = 	ext{polylog}(|G|)$.
main_assumptions: The algorithms rely on specific structural assumptions about the groups (e.g., quasi-Hamiltonian structure, or $A$ having bounded generator rank) and assume black-box access to group operations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the inclusion relationship between various group classes: Nilpotent $\le 2$, Quasi-Hamiltonian, Dedekind, and Abelian groups.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the context of HSP difficulty in non-Abelian settings. It then details algorithms for semidirect products (Theorem A/B), followed by a dedicated treatment for quasi-Hamiltonian groups (Theorem C). The latter sections involve deep analysis of quantum measurement protocols (PGM) and structural comparisons with other group families.
why_interesting: This work pushes the boundaries of quantum complexity theory by extending known quantum algorithms beyond simple Abelian structures to complex, structured non-Abelian groups relevant in abstract algebra.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic inclusion relations among several classes of groups. The class Nil≤2 includes the groups of nilpotency class ≤2. For these groups, the algorithm of [15] solves the HSP efficiently. The nilpotency class of quasi-Hamiltonian groups is not bounded by a constant and therefore these two classes are incomparable (see Appendix A). Both classes contain the finite Dedekind groups, in which every subgroup is normal. Note that the dihedral group DN is nilpotent if and only if N is a power of two.
